issues.explanation: The invite form renders @error('inviteRole') but no @error('inviteEmail') block, so an invite-email validation error may not render exactly once as required (old template needed an explicit @error).
Task requires both the Livewire component and the entity.members route to 403 for employees, but change.diff contains no routes change to verify route-level enforcement.
Server-context record id is client-writable without #[Locked]; saveRole() trusts it (scoped to own entity via findOrFail, so impact is limited to managers).
UI-state actions reset modal state without server-side authorization, violating every-action-authorizes policy (no DB write, so low risk).
Project pattern is #[Validate] plus $this->validate(); this calls validateOnly twice, which deviates and can mishandle multi-field error state.
Subject uses a translatable key but lang/pt_BR.json has no entry for it, so the pt-BR subject stays English.

conventions.evidence: app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:42 #[Validate] inviteEmail/inviteRole/memberRole; EntityInvite #[Fillable] explicit; migration up()/down() reversible; Log::channel('audit'); docs/CHANGELOG updated; deviations: validateOnly x2 vs $this->validate(), domain write inline not via app/Actions (matches old sibling style)

review.summary: The change implements invite-only membership end to end: normalized entity_invites table, rate-limited sendInvite with race-safe replace, email-matched accept/decline, manager-only members page with detail and removal modals, translated mail and UI, plus broad Pest coverage. It needs changes before merging because the invite-email error block is missing from the Blade and route-level manager-only enforcement is not evidenced, with smaller Livewire hardening nits.
